edits.before: The code calls $\beta=1/(2\sigma^2)$. Increasing beta narrows the row and lowers entropy. `row_at_beta` subtracts the smallest squared distance before exponentiating; this common shift cancels in normalization and stops all weights from underflowing together. `solve_row` brackets beta, bisects once an upper bound exists and reports a status after a bounded number of iterations. It ignores zero-probability terms when evaluating $p\log p$, whose limiting value is 0. Uniform input scaling by $c>0$ divides beta by $c^2$ at the same target and preserves the row.

edits.before: Diffusion coordinates weight walk eigenmodes by $\lambda_l^t$ at a chosen time $t$. For an undirected positive-degree graph, the symmetric-normalized operator provides real modes that can be converted to right eigenvectors of the walk. The complete `diffusion_coordinates` function above removes stationary modes and ranks other modes by absolute eigenvalue. The chain has a−1 mode: without self loops the walk is periodic. A lazy transition $(I+P_{walk})/2$ would remove that particular alternation, but it is a changed walk and must be named. There is no scikit-learn `DiffusionMap` call invented here; the exact tiny walk and numerical eigensolver are the computational route.

Keep a shared symmetric half-bound M in the state, initially4. After each finite positive-rate Step and its reported centroid subtraction, set M←max(M,ceil(max_i|y_i|)). Drawing extents include all current and compared endpoints and disclose a scale extension; they cannot silently crop the failed step. Keep scale and M fixed throughout a drag/edit and on ID changes.
